```{r}

# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggpubr)
library(readxl)

# Set working directory and file path
setwd("~/R")
file_path <- "Rodrigo_Clean_data.xlsx"

# Read data, remove missing values, and convert specified columns to factors
data_cleaned <- read_excel(file_path, sheet = "Sheet1") %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  mutate(
    blinding_practice = as.factor(blinding_practice),
    treatment_lines = as.factor(treatment_lines),
    disease_status = as.factor(disease_status),
    sponsors = as.factor(sponsors),
    trial_location = as.factor(trial_location),
    site_number = as.factor(site_number),
  )

# Create derived variables: non_compliance, death_rate, and TRAE_rate
data_cleaned <- data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    non_compliance = ifelse(
      total_number_enrolled > 0,
      (total_withdrew_noreason + total_withdrew_because_noncompliance + lost_fu) / total_number_enrolled,
      NA
    ),
    death_rate = ifelse(
      total_number_enrolled > 0,
      total_withdrew_because_death / total_number_enrolled,
      NA
    ),
    TRAE_rate = ifelse(
      total_number_withdrew > 0,
      total_withdrew_because_ae / total_number_withdrew,
      NA
    )
  ) %>%
  # Filter out rows with missing non_compliance or death_rate, rename non_compliance to outcome
  filter(!is.na(non_compliance), !is.na(death_rate)) %>%
  rename(outcome = non_compliance)

# Add a binary variable for unclear follow-up status
data_cleaned <- data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    unclear_follow_up_boolean = ifelse(outcome > 0.15, "Above 15%", "15% or Below")
  )

# Rename values in the blinding_practice column
# Convert control_group to a categorical variable and relabel values if needed
data_cleaned <- data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    blinding_practice = case_when(
      blinding_practice == 1 ~ "patient_blind",
      blinding_practice %in% c(2, 3) ~ "patient_aware",
      TRUE ~ as.character(blinding_practice)  # Keep other values unchanged
    ),
    control_group = as.factor(control_group)  # Convert control_group to factor
  )

# Perform Wilcoxon rank-sum tests for numeric variables
wilcox_results <- list(
  follow_up = wilcox.test(follow_up_period ~ unclear_follow_up_boolean, data = data_cleaned),
  TEAEs = wilcox.test(TRAE_rate ~ unclear_follow_up_boolean, data = data_cleaned),
  deaths = wilcox.test(death_rate ~ unclear_follow_up_boolean, data = data_cleaned)
)

# Perform chi-squared or Fisher's exact test depending on expected frequencies
chi_squared_results <- lapply(categorical_vars, function(var) {
  contingency_table <- table(data_cleaned[[var]], data_cleaned$unclear_follow_up_boolean)
  
  # Check if any expected frequency is below 5
  if (any(prop.table(contingency_table) * sum(contingency_table) < 5)) {
    test_result <- fisher.test(contingency_table)  # Use Fisher's exact test
  } else {
    test_result <- chisq.test(contingency_table)  # Use Chi-squared test
  }
  
  return(test_result)
})

# Combine results for categorical variables into a named list
names(chi_squared_results) <- categorical_vars


# Create boxplots for numeric variables
boxplots <- list(
  follow_up = ggboxplot(data_cleaned, x = "unclear_follow_up_boolean", y = "follow_up_period",
                        color = "unclear_follow_up_boolean", title = "Follow-Up Period by Unclear Follow-Up Status",
                        ylab = "Follow-Up Period", xlab = "Unclear Follow-Up Status"),
  TEAEs = ggboxplot(data_cleaned, x = "unclear_follow_up_boolean", y = "TRAE_rate",
                    color = "unclear_follow_up_boolean", title = "TEAEs by Unclear Follow-Up Status",
                    ylab = "TEAEs Rate", xlab = "Unclear Follow-Up Status"),
  deaths = ggboxplot(data_cleaned, x = "unclear_follow_up_boolean", y = "death_rate",
                     color = "unclear_follow_up_boolean", title = "Death Rate by Unclear Follow-Up Status",
                     ylab = "Death Rate", xlab = "Unclear Follow-Up Status")
)


lapply(boxplots, print)

# Extract p-values and test types from chi_squared_results
categorical_p_values <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(chi_squared_results),
  P_Value = sapply(chi_squared_results, function(result) result$p.value),
  Test_Type = sapply(chi_squared_results, function(result) {
    if ("method" %in% names(result)) {
      result$method
    } else {
      "Unknown"
    }
  }),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Extract p-values and test types from wilcox_results
wilcox_p_values <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(wilcox_results),
  P_Value = sapply(wilcox_results, function(result) result$p.value),
  Test_Type = rep("Wilcoxon rank-sum test", length(wilcox_results)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Combine both results into a single table
combined_p_values <- rbind(categorical_p_values, wilcox_p_values)

# Sort table by Variable name for clarity (optional)
combined_p_values <- combined_p_values[order(combined_p_values$Variable), ]

# Display the combined table
print(combined_p_values)

# Optionally, write the combined table to an Excel file
library(writexl)
write_xlsx(combined_p_values, "Combined_P_Values.xlsx")
```


```{r}
#Regression

# Load necessary libraries
library(readxl)     # To read Excel files
library(dplyr)      # For data manipulation
library(mgcv)       # For GAM modeling
library(caret)      # For splitting data
library(ggplot2)    # For data visualization

# Step 1: Read the data and remove missing values
file_path <- "Rodrigo_Clean_data.xlsx"  # File path
data <- read_excel(file_path, sheet = "Sheet1") %>%
  na.omit()  # Remove rows with missing values

# Step 2: Convert categorical variables to factors
data_cleaned <- data %>%
  mutate(
    treatment_lines = as.factor(treatment_lines),
    tx_group_drug = as.factor(tx_group_drug),
    sponsors = as.factor(sponsors)
  )

# Step 3: Create derived variables (`non_compliance` and `death_rate`)
if (all(c("total_withdrew_noreason", "total_withdrew_because_noncompliance", "lost_fu", "total_number_enrolled") %in% colnames(data_cleaned))) {
  data_cleaned <- data_cleaned %>%
    mutate(
      non_compliance = ifelse(
        total_number_enrolled > 0,
        (total_withdrew_noreason + total_withdrew_because_noncompliance + lost_fu) / total_number_enrolled,
        NA
      )
    )
}

if (all(c("total_withdrew_because_death", "total_number_enrolled") %in% colnames(data_cleaned))) {
  data_cleaned <- data_cleaned %>%
    mutate(
      death_rate = ifelse(
        total_number_enrolled > 0,
        total_withdrew_because_death / total_number_enrolled,
        NA
      )
    )
}

# Calculate TRAE_rate as the ratio of total_withdrew_because_ae to total_number_withdrew
data_cleaned <- data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(TRAE_rate = ifelse(total_number_withdrew > 0, 
                            total_withdrew_because_ae / total_number_withdrew, 
                            NA))  # Handle cases where denominator is zero

# Remove rows with missing `non_compliance` or `death_rate`
data_cleaned <- data_cleaned %>%
  filter(!is.na(non_compliance), !is.na(death_rate)) %>%
  rename(outcome = non_compliance)  # Rename `non_compliance` to `outcome`

# Step 4: Split data into training, validation, and test sets
set.seed(123)
train_index <- createDataPartition(data_cleaned$outcome, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- data_cleaned[train_index, ]
remaining_data <- data_cleaned[-train_index, ]

validation_index <- createDataPartition(remaining_data$outcome, p = 0.5, list = FALSE)
validation_data <- remaining_data[validation_index, ]
test_data <- remaining_data[-validation_index, ]

# Check for missing values in the data
sum(is.na(data_cleaned))
sum(is.na(train_data$outcome))
sum(is.na(validation_data$outcome))
sum(is.na(test_data$outcome))

# Remove rows with NA outcomes or predictors using filter()
train_data <- train_data %>% filter(complete.cases(.))
validation_data <- validation_data %>% filter(complete.cases(.))
test_data <- test_data %>% filter(complete.cases(.))

# Step 5: Visualize relationships between predictors and `outcome`
numeric_vars <- c("follow_up_period", "TRAE_rate", "death_rate")

for (var in numeric_vars) {
  p <- ggplot(data_cleaned, aes(x = .data[[var]], y = outcome)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "blue") +  # Linear fit
    geom_smooth(method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "tp"), color = "red") +  # GAM fit
    labs(title = paste("Relationship between", var, "and Outcome"),
         x = var, y = "Outcome") +
    theme_minimal()
  print(p)
}

# Step 6: Fit the GAM model
gam_model <- gam(
  formula = outcome ~ 
     randomization+ s(follow_up_period, bs = "tp")+s(TRAE_rate, bs = "tp")+
    s(death_rate, bs = "tp"), 
  data = train_data,
  family = gaussian(link = "log")  # Log link for nonlinear relationship
)

# Step 7: Evaluate the model
# Generate predictions
train_data$predicted_outcome <- predict(gam_model, newdata = train_data)
validation_data$predicted_outcome <- predict(gam_model, newdata = validation_data)
test_data$predicted_outcome <- predict(gam_model, newdata = test_data)

# Define RMSE function
calculate_rmse <- function(observed, predicted) {
  sqrt(mean((observed - predicted)^2))
}

# Calculate RMSE (back-transform predictions for log link)
train_rmse <- calculate_rmse(train_data$outcome, exp(train_data$predicted_outcome))
validation_rmse <- calculate_rmse(validation_data$outcome, exp(validation_data$predicted_outcome))
test_rmse <- calculate_rmse(test_data$outcome, exp(test_data$predicted_outcome))

# Calculate baseline RMSE
baseline_prediction <- mean(data_cleaned$outcome)
baseline_rmse <- calculate_rmse(test_data$outcome, baseline_prediction)

# Step 8: Compare RMSE to baseline and variance
outcome_sd <- sd(data_cleaned$outcome)
outcome_range <- max(data_cleaned$outcome) - min(data_cleaned$outcome)

cat("Baseline RMSE:", baseline_rmse, "\n")
cat("Outcome Standard Deviation (SD):", outcome_sd, "\n")
cat("Outcome Range:", outcome_range, "\n")

# Relative RMSE
train_rrmse <- train_rmse / mean(train_data$outcome)
validation_rrmse <- validation_rmse / mean(validation_data$outcome)
test_rrmse <- test_rmse / mean(test_data$outcome)

results <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("RMSE", "RRMSE"),
  Train = c(train_rmse, train_rrmse),
  Validation = c(validation_rmse, validation_rrmse),
  Test = c(test_rmse, test_rrmse),
  Baseline = c(baseline_rmse, baseline_rmse / mean(data_cleaned$outcome))
)
print(results)

# Step 9: Visualize Observed vs Predicted for Test Set
ggplot(test_data, aes(x = exp(predicted_outcome), y = outcome)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Observed vs Predicted Outcomes - Test Set",
    x = "Predicted Outcome",
    y = "Observed Outcome"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Summary of GAM model
summary(gam_model)
```




```{r}
#Assessment for confounding


ggplot(data_cleaned, aes(x = outcome, y = TRAE_rate)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "blue") +
    labs(title = "TRAEs vs Non-Compliance", x = "Non-Compliance", y = "TRAE Rate")


#Add interaction term

gam_model <- gam(
  formula = outcome ~ randomization + s(follow_up_period, bs = "tp") +
             s(TRAE_rate, bs = "tp") + s(death_rate, bs = "tp") +
             TRAE_rate:follow_up_period,
  data = train_data,
  family = gaussian(link = "log")
)
summary(gam_model)

# Generate predictions for the test set
test_data$predicted_outcome <- predict(gam_model, newdata = test_data, type = "response")

# Create the plot
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(test_data, aes(x = predicted_outcome, y = outcome)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, color = "blue") +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Observed vs Predicted Outcomes",
    x = "Predicted Outcome",
    y = "Observed Outcome"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12)
  )

#Invesigate non-linearity
plot(gam_model, select = 2, pages = 1)  # TRAE_rate
plot(gam_model, select = 1, pages = 1)  # follow_up_period


```
